text: Harbour City started strong and scored two goals first! Elias Okafor and Marek Barros helped make it 2-0 by halftime [#905] [#975]. But Seabrook Town didn’t give up—they played wide and fast to score four goals and win 4-2 [#1104] [#1448] [#1882]. The last two goals by Kian Romano were like quick lightning strikes at the end of the game! [#1906]. Marek Barros from Harbour City was a star player with lots of passes and a great game [#975]. The teams played with cool strategies: Harbour City liked short passes, and Seabrook Town used wide crossing plays to trick their opponents [#1361]. In the end, Seabrook Town’s energy and teamwork helped them turn the game around in an exciting finish!

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for kid audience in en

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals in total, coming from a higher xG of 3.48 compared to Harbour City's 1.0, leading to their 4-2 win [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros (Harbour City) was the player of the match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and a 9.8 rating, despite his team's loss [#975].
- Harbour City led 2-0 early in the game with goals at 45' and 47', but Seabrook Town came back strongly in the second half [#905, #975, #1104, #1448].
- Seabrook Town made a tactical change at 65' with more pressing and direct play, which led to increased chances and goals in the second half [#1361, #1448].
- Late goals by Kian Romano at 90+2' and 90+3' secured the victory for Seabrook Town, extending their lead from 3-2 to 4-2 in stoppage time [#1882, #1906].

- Seabrook Town exploited their wide, crossing play style (3-4-3 formation) to create high-quality attacking chances, as shown by their higher xG (3.48 vs 1.0) and more box touches (57 vs 42), indicating effective penetration in attacking areas [team_stats].
- Harbour City’s patient short passing approach (4-2-3-1 formation) is reflected in their extensive buildup to Okafor’s goal (17 passes over 56.7 seconds) using short through balls to unlock the defense, showing their controlled possession and calculated chance creation [goal at 45', evidence 904,905].
- Seabrook Town’s goals late in the game (90+2' and 90+3') came from quick counter-attacks following regains with low-duration possession sequences, highlighting an adjustment to a more direct style to capitalize on Harbour City’s higher press and line (tactical changes at 65' and 90+2') [goal at 90+2', evidence 1881,1882].
- Harbour City’s tactical change late on to press higher and play more direct (90+2') reflects a reactive approach to chasing the game, but this increased directness coincided with conceding the leading and final goals, showing a struggle to adapt under pressure [tactical change 90+2', evidence 1884].
